text.p: The Turkish central bank lent banks 17.3 trillion lira overnight cash at 75 percent on Tuesday, after Monday's 17.8 trillion lira, to ease a persisting liquidity squeeze.
Overnight money also traded at 74.75 percent during the day.
Turkish lira weakened sharply to 97,340 against the dollar from Monday's 96,850 close after the Treasury sold only 39.23 trillion lira nominal-valued 273-day bills in an auction.
Bankers said the lira weakened on expectations of easier money rates for tomorrow.

Banks will pay the Treasury 21.4 trillion lira for the auction on Wednesday in return for 96.15 trillion lira of t-bill maturities which will leave a net surplus of about 75 trillion lira in the money market.
The lira dived to a low of 97,350 per dollar on auction results from around 97,100 before closing at 97,340.

T-bill and bond yields which dropped by up to two points on continued buying in the morning, further slipped after the auction where the Treasury cut the maximum yield by 3.58 points from the previous auction to 118.75 percent.
The average yield on the most heavily traded October 30, 1997 bonds shrank to 111.64 percent with Wednesday value after the auction, from today's 111.87 percent and Monday's 113.90.
The second most active June 4, 1997 bills yielded an average 109.55 percent with Wednesday value after the auction, down from today's 111.15 and Monday's 113.05 percent.

August 6, 1997 bills sold in the auction will be the first to be subject to a newly imposed 10 percent witholding tax on interest income in 1997. The tax does not apply to outstanding papers having 1997 maturities.
Bankers said the imposing of the witholding tax caused total bids to dive to 244 trillion lira in the auction from a record of around 1,000 trillion in the previous one-year bond auction.
The August 6 papers were not traded after the auction.
